text:
lina: quick sync — customer requests for private deployments are converging into two nagging asks: 1) customer-managed networking (preserve egress IPs / peering permanence) and 2) zero-downtime in-place upgrades for operator-managed installs. want to propose a prioritized roadmap slice for Q2 that targets both. :eyes:
raj: can you break down the real engineering scope for each? rough bullet points is fine.
jess: fyi field has 6 customers asking about egress IP preservation specifically — mainly for firewall allowlists and IP-based auditing. one large bank needs it non-negotiable.
lina: sure — rough: 
- customer-managed networking: installer provides "hosted control plane + networking handover hooks" (BGP / static peering docs, preserve node egress IP via SNAT policy) + explicit handshake UX for netops.
- in-place upgrades: operator upgrades that don't replace tenant IPs, migrate CRDs gracefully, and fallback to previous control plane if post-upgrade health checks fail.
thomas: engineering concerns: upgrading without replacing node egress IPs depends on how the CNI manages allocation. for on-prem we probably need a mode that uses the host's IP masquerade rules instead of recreating interfaces. that has ops/security implications.
raj: timeline estimates (very rough): 
- networking handover API + docs: 3-4 wks (core impl 2w + docs/tests 1-2w)
- SNAT/preserve mode: 4-6 wks (CNI shim + tests)
- in-place operator upgrade flow: 6-8 wks (canary rollout hooks, CRD migration tooling)
jess: any low-friction mitigations we can offer customers now? templates, runbooks, or a consultative service?
lina: yes — offer a "netops handoff kit" (runbook + example iptables/SNAT snippets + support hour credit). cheap and de-risks early adopters.
thomas: also propose a fallback pattern: deploy a lightweight sidecar proxy as temporary bridge for IP preservation while the long-term SNAT mode is matured. tradeoff: more complexity and latency.
raj: can we scope a minimal viable shipping criteria? e.g., 
- MVS for networking: documented handoff steps, 2 customer validations, automated test that asserts stable egress IP across restart
- MVS for upgrades: automated canary flow, rollback trigger on health failure, and one customer pilot pass
- security review signoff (SRE + Sec)
lina: agree. add performance SLAs: upgrades shouldn't increase tail latency beyond +10% for request path during canary windows.
jess: field asks we track: regulator bank (preserve IPs), media company (minimal outage during nightly patching), healthcare customer (audit logs + KMS integration).
infra-bot: CI: packaging-integration — 1 failed test (operator-upgrade-canary) — https://ci.internal/packaging/879 — error: timeout on CRD migration.
thomas: ok noted, that failure is expected for current branch. we need dedicated e2e for CRD migrations before we call upgrade flow stable.
raj: dependency list: CNI shim, operator canary hooks, installer handshake UX, docs/runbooks, e2e suites, security review.
lina: prioritization proposal (vote): 
- P0: SNAT/preserve mode + docs + runbook (customer-facing deliverable)
- P1: operator in-place upgrade automation + canary/rollback tooling
- P2: sidecar bridge and advanced networking templates (opt-in)
- P3: additional features (bgp automation, ipam integrations)
jess: :thumbsup: P0 first please. customers pushing.
thomas: echo. but engineering asks that we run the SNAT work concurrently with a spike on CRD migration patterns so we don't block upgrades later. estimate extra 1 week of overlap cost.
lina: decision: prioritize P0 and start spike for CRD migration in parallel. owners: SNAT engineer = @raj, docs+runbook = @jess, upgrade canary spike = @thomas. target: customer pilot for SNAT in 6 weeks, public runbook the same week.
raj: I'll open the RFC and link the implementation plan. will include a minimal config example: 
```yaml
installerProfiles:
  - name: "host-networking-handshake"
    networkingMode: "preserve-egress"
    preserveEgress: true
    egressIpHint: "10.0.0.5"  # optional, used for docs/testing
```
jess: I'll draft runbook + customer checklist. will request pilot slots from the field next week.
thomas: I'll attach the CRD migration test plan to the RFC. will also stub the canary rollback hook in the operator.
lina: thanks — I'll add this to the roadmap board and book a 30m sync next Tue to review RFC + pilot invites. tagging leadership for awareness: @ops-lead please note potential bank customer requirement.
jess: noted. putting bank on the pilot contact list.
lina: end state we want: customers can opt into "preserve-egress" at install time, upgrades are non-disruptive, and field has prescriptive runbooks so support load is predictable. any objections?
thomas: none. raising a follow-up: test matrix for cloud-proxy and NAT edge cases.
raj: no objections. will prioritize.
jess: no objections. :white_check_mark:
lina: great — thanks all. action items summarized: 
- raj: RFC + impl plan (due in 5 days)
- jess: runbook + pilot coordination (due in 7 days)
- thomas: CRD migration spike + test plan (due in 7 days)
- infra-bot: run packaging-integration on SNAT branch daily until pilot

lina: we'll reconvene Tue 09:30 PT.
